summary: Initial discovery for migrating Archon Labs from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. Main concerns: eval parity (instruction following / hallucination), latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC and KMS integration, and compatibility with existing vLLM/TGI-based infra. Redwood AE+SE outlined Dedicated features, routing/fallback options, and proposed benchmarks. Agreed next steps: pricing, run benchmarks, technical deep dive.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46 min | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (CTO - Archon), Sofia Ramirez (ML Eng), Daniel Park (Security), Lena Ortiz (Product)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, with Priya on the technical side. How's everybody doing?
[00:12] Marcus Lee: Good, thanks. Quick background — we've been on OpenAI for generation and embeddings, plus some homegrown vLLM instances for lower-latency internal infra. Looking to understand Dedicated and private options.
[00:28] Priya Natarajan: Great, thanks Marcus. Could you run through your current volume, latency needs, and any compliance constraints?
[00:36] Sofia Ramirez: Sure. We do about 20M generation tokens/mo, 1M embeddings, p95 latency target is ~200ms for short chat flows. For some batch jobs we care more about throughput. We have PII in a few prompts so need either VPC or on-prem options and KMS for keys.
[00:54] Daniel Park: From security perspective we need SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, and customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS). Also audit logs retained for 1 year.
[01:08] Alex Chen: That's helpful — Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and a private control plane; KMS integrations and HSM are options. We also provide audit logs and can map RBAC to SAML groups. We'll share the compliance pack.
[01:22] Marcus Lee: Great. A couple of things: we've optimized some models with vLLM and TGI and have custom tokenizers. How compatible is Redwood with those artifacts?
[01:34] Priya Natarajan: Good question. Redwood supports model variants and common model formats — we run a compatibility pass during onboarding. For vLLM/TGI setups, kernel/runtime differences matter; priors like kv cache behavior and attention optimizations can shift latency and exact eval scores. We typically validate parity with an eval suite.
[01:53] Marcus Lee: By parity you mean instruction-following and hallucination rates?
[01:58] Priya Natarajan: Exactly. We'll run your eval set against the target model on our Dedicated fleet and compare metrics: F1, BLEU-ish heuristics, hallucination counts, and latency/throughput. Sometimes tokenization differences change embedding similarity, so we check that too.
[02:15] Lena Ortiz: Do you have an example deck or benchmark template?
[02:18] Alex Chen: Yes — we'll send a benchmark template and our recommended test scripts (see placeholder link we will share: https://redwood.example/decks/dedicated-benchmarks).
[02:30] Speaker 2: sorry, I joined late can you repeat the scope?
[02:33] Marcus Lee: We're talking migration away from OpenAI hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated to get predictable costs and private networking, plus integrating our vLLM/TGI optimizations.
[02:45] Priya Natarajan: One note: some models on OpenAI have proprietary instruction-tuning behaviors; when we run open models the outputs can be slightly different. We work with model variants and quantization profiles to get as close as possible.
[03:02] Sofia Ramirez: Are there known regressions when switching from OpenAI gpt-4 style to an open model on Dedicated? We saw some throughput gains with TGI but the hallucination rate changed.
[03:15] Priya Natarajan: There can be regressions depending on model choice and tokenization. Our approach is to run head-to-head evals and then tune quantization and kernel params. Also caching — Redwood's prefix/KV caching helps reduce cost and can improve p95 latency for repeated contexts.
[03:34] Marcus Lee: How does Redwood handle fallback if our Dedicated capacity is saturated? We have bursty traffic.
[03:40] Alex Chen: You can configure routing policies — primary to Dedicated, fallback to hosted Redwood variants in a different region/tier, or even to a lower-cost model. We also support burst capacity and autoscaling rules.
[03:56] Daniel Park: On keys: we want to ensure tokens are never stored unencrypted and that we control KMS keys. Is that supported?
[04:03] Priya Natarajan: Yes — customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated; keys can be in your cloud KMS or an HSM. At rest data is encrypted and we can disable retention of request/response payloads if necessary.
[04:18] Alex Chen: For the business side, we usually propose a pilot on Dedicated with a committed baseline, then bump to reserved if you see sustained usage. Pricing and committed capacity details we'll share after this call.
[04:32] Marcus Lee: Good. Timeframes: we want to decide in Q4 and ideally roll out a pilot in January. Is that realistic?
[04:40] Alex Chen: Definitely doable — onboarding for Dedicated typically takes 4-8 weeks depending on network/entitlement approvals.
[04:49] Speaker 2: there's a slide about eval parity?
[04:52] Priya Natarajan: Yes — our eval plan includes tokenization checks, embeddings similarity thresholds, hallucination audits, latency and cost per token. We can also bring in performance engineers to tune vLLM/TGI-specific kernels if needed.
[05:08] Marcus Lee: For the vLLM/TGI instances we run ourselves — can we reuse the same compiled kernels or do we need to recompile?
[05:16] Priya Natarajan: You'll likely need a build/profile pass — Redwood's runtime selects kernels based on architecture and sequence length distribution. If you have custom kernels we can evaluate compatibility; sometimes small changes are required.
[05:30] Sofia Ramirez: About embeddings parity — we depend on exact cosine similarity thresholds from our retrieval pipeline. Tokenization differences break results. How do you address that?
[05:40] Priya Natarajan: We run the same tokenizer pipeline during onboarding and recommend pinning tokenizer versions. For critical flows we can run a migration test: compare similarity matrices on a held-out set and quantify delta. If deltas are unacceptable, we iterate on model variant or quantization.
[05:58] Marcus Lee: Any red flags from Redwood's side for our current infra?
[06:03] Alex Chen: Nothing major; just planning on the devops side: VPC peering, KMS provisioning, and SAML config are the usual gating items. We can provide a network checklist.
[06:17] Daniel Park: About audit logs retention — is 1 year supported out-of-the-box or an add-on?
[06:22] Priya Natarajan: We have both short-term and long-term retention options. 1 year is available as an add-on for Dedicated / Private. We'll include specifics in the compliance docs.
[06:36] Lena Ortiz: On costs: can you give a ballpark cost delta comparing OpenAI hosted vs Redwood Dedicated with reserved capacity?
[06:45] Alex Chen: Ballpark depends on model and commit levels. For high-token workloads Dedicated usually yields 30-60% lower unit costs once you bake in reserved capacity and optimizations like quantization and caching. We'll send pricing scenarios.
[06:58] Marcus Lee: What about model updates — if we want to swap model versions mid-flight, how do rollouts look?
[07:04] Priya Natarajan: We support canary rollouts, A/B testing, and automatic fallback policies. The console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route.
[07:18] Marcus Lee: For models that were tuned on OpenAI's infrastructure, will we be allowed to run those weights on Dedicated?
[07:26] Priya Natarajan: If you own the weights and licensing permits, yes. We also support bringing your own model artifacts. We'll perform an onboarding compatibility check.
[07:35] Sofia Ramirez: Any known gotchas moving from OpenAI embeddings to an open LLM embeddings on Redwood?
[07:41] Priya Natarajan: The common issue is vector drift due to training differences. Our eval checks focus on similarity calibration; sometimes we recommend a small reindex or recalibration of thresholds.
[07:54] Marcus Lee: On the technical deep dive, can we include an engineer who set up vLLM at our company? They want to discuss kernel tuning.
[08:01] Alex Chen: Absolutely — we'll loop in a performance engineer.
[08:06] Marcus Lee: Great. Are there case studies for customers who migrated from OpenAI to Redwood?
[08:11] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll share a short case study and a migration checklist.
[08:16] Daniel Park: Any SOC2 or ISO reports accessible?
[08:19] Alex Chen: We'll send the SOC2 attestation and other compliance artifacts to Daniel.
[08:23] Speaker 2: quick Q — where does Redwood Optimize fit in?
[08:27] Priya Natarajan: Redwood Optimize gives batching/quantization suggestions and model recommendations per workload to cut unit cost while meeting SLOs. It's integrated in the console.
[08:37] Marcus Lee: For the benchmark — what should we provide vs what Redwood will run?
[08:42] Priya Natarajan: Provide sample prompts, evaluation labels, and any constraints (latency thresholds). We'll run the same prompts on your OpenAI baseline and on candidate models in Dedicated and share results.
[08:55] Marcus Lee: Any limits on model sizes for Dedicated?
[08:59] Priya Natarajan: We support a range of model sizes; largest models may need multi-GPU sharding. We'll recommend instance types for your workload.
[09:08] Lena Ortiz: About procurement — what does contracting look like?
[09:12] Alex Chen: Standard enterprise contract with an SOW for Dedicated onboarding, plus options for reserved capacity. We'll share a redline-friendly template.
[09:22] Marcus Lee: If we do a pilot, will Redwood help with A/Bing against OpenAI?
[09:26] Priya Natarajan: Yes, we can run comparative tests and produce a regression report.
[09:33] Speaker 2: sorry, small tangent — did you say support for HSM?
[09:36] Daniel Park: yes, HSM/KMS support is key.
[09:39] Priya Natarajan: Confirmed — HSM integrations supported for Private and Dedicated.
[09:45] Marcus Lee: Any latency tradeoffs when using KMS for every request?
[09:49] Priya Natarajan: Typically we only call KMS for key decryption at startup or token rotation, not per-request. So KMS shouldn't add per-request latency. We'll confirm with security docs.
[09:59] Alex Chen: Quick recap — Redwood will: send pricing + contract template, send compliance pack (SOC2, encryption), provide benchmark template and script, schedule technical deep dive. Archon will: share prompts, sample eval set, and security questions.
[10:15] Marcus Lee: Sounds good. Is there anything else we should consider around vLLM?
[10:19] Priya Natarajan: Just that while vLLM/TGI can be very fast, the runtime and kernel choices can change outputs. That's why the eval is important. We can also co-tune kernels if needed.
[10:31] Lena Ortiz: Timeline OK — we'll try to have sample dataset and legal contacts by next week.
[10:36] Alex Chen: Great. We'll set up follow-ups — one technical deep dive with Priya and performance team, and one procurement sync.
[10:45] Marcus Lee: Thanks, everyone.
[10:47] Daniel Park: Thanks.
[46:00] End meeting: notes saved and action items captured.

References / Shared artifacts: Redwood Dedicated overview deck (link to be sent), benchmark template (link), SOC2 attestation (to be shared via secure link). Some transcription artifacts: occasional speaker mislabels and filler words retained.
